THIS year, 10,000 schoolboys and schoolgirls were so interested in cookery as a hobby or as a career that they entered the 1961 Children's Electric Cooking Competition organised by the South of Scotland Electricity Board. From a modest start in 1952 this competition has become an important annual event in the South of Scotland.

location_standardised: Glasgow, Glasgow City, Scotland, United Kingdom
brief_context: City where young men are training as chefs.
brief_extract: From the results of this competition and previous competitions, it certainly looks as though Scotland is likely to command the kitchen in the future as well as the engine room. I was indeed interested to learn that in Glasgow at present there are six young men training as chefs whose introduction to cookery was through the Electric Cooking Competition. As would be expected, the girl competitors usually considerably outnumber the boys, but this does not mean that the standard of the boys' cooking is not equally as high as the girls'.

location_standardised: Kelvin Hall, Glasgow, Glasgow City, Scotland, United Kingdom
brief_context: The venue for the competition's Grand Final.
brief_extract: Plans are laid in March of each year and all schools have to be notified of the arrangements before the summer holidays begin. Immediately after the closing date for entries in September the local heats are held; these are followed by Area semi-finals and then comes the Grand Final in Kelvin Hall, Glasgow, towards the end of October, coinciding usually with the Modern Homes Exhibition, equivalent to the Ideal Home Exhibition. Savings Certificates are awarded as prizes in the Area contests and at the Grand Final the first three boys and the first three girls receive prizes worth £20, £10 and £5.

We walked up and down the two rows of candidates watching the deft little pairs of hands mashing potatoes, carefully breaking eggs (no bad ones marred the evening or the reputation of the producers), slicing tomatoes and lovingly decorating their dishes to make them look as appetising as possible for our benefit.

ELECTRICITE DE FRANCE arranged my tour

great cross-section of people, ranging from the
sophisticated and speedy life of the Parisian to
the simple life of the rural areas. Since the electricity undertakings were na-

in electrification, but the mass destruction of the
war left great problems, so that the selling of
electrical appliances is often hampered by lack
of supply in the older parts of the larger towns.

article_title: Advertisement: Kedleston Hall - Historic House Tours
brief_extract: Built 1757-1765 on the site of the original XIIth Century manor—Kedleston with its world-famous Marble Hall and magnificent State Rooms, is the finest untouched example of the work of Robert Adam in the country, and houses an important collection of old masters and contemporary furniture. Visitors can also see the famous collection of Indian Treasures—Silver—Ivories—Antique Weapons—Spears—Poisoned Arrows etc., made by the Marquis Curzon of Kedleston while Viceroy of India, 1898-1905, and the XIIth Century Church and Curzon Memorial Chapel. OPEN - Good Friday to Wednesday.

location_standardised: Leeds, West Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location of the first all-teachers EAW branch.
article_title: The EAW and the Professional Woman
brief_extract: has recently been breaking some exciting new ground in Yorkshire. Over a year ago we formed our first all-teachers branch in Leeds. This was followed in February of this year by the formation of another branch in Sheffield specifically for teachers and for other professional and business women who are interested in studying the ways in which electricity can help in their jobs as well as in their homes.

location_standardised: Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, United Kingdom
brief_context: Location where a specialist EAW branch was recently formed.
article_title: The EAW and the Professional Woman
brief_extract: Over a year ago we formed our first all-teachers branch in Leeds. This was followed in February of this year by the formation of another branch in Sheffield specifically for teachers and for other professional and business women who are interested in studying the ways in which electricity can help in their jobs as well as in their homes. We have, of course, always numbered professional and business women among our members, but this is the first time that such women have been encouraged to form their own separate branches.

article_title: A Health Visitor looks at . . . SAFETY IN THE HOME
brief_extract:
H. KANE, H.V., who holds a Parentcraft Teaching Certificate and Diploma in Sociology (London)
describes the conditions in many homes
THE surprising thing about electrical accidents in the home is that there are not many more of them. The general assumption seems to be that electrical equipment, whatever its condition, is all right until it goes all wrong; that the accidents you hear about happen to other people, not to you; that the advice attached to electrical equipment and the posters on safety seen in the clinic and similar places are to be taken in the same way as the headlines in the more notorious daily papers.

Members visited the offices and printing works of this newspaper which has one of the largest circulations in the Midlands. brief_context: Region from which specialist guests are drawn.
article_title: Behind the Scenes on Television Gardening Club
brief_extract:
Percy Thrower have done
their best to present good sound gardening in-
formation to the viewers in an interesting and
acceptable manner. To assist in this, specialist
guests have been drawn from all parts of the
British Isles; Scotland, Wales and Ireland have
been represented as well as England, and a
gardener was brought from as far away as the
Isle of Arran to show the tender trees and
shrubs that grow on the island under the soften-
ing influence of the Gulf Stream on its climate. The object of the programme is to help gar-
deners with their problems, by demonstrating
the proper way of performing routine tasks, by
showing them which are the best and most suit-
able plants for various situations, and offering
them instruction on the cultivation of fruits
and vegetables.

brief_context: Used in a comparison for the type of count down.
brief_extract: The studio manager dons his headphones through which he is in contact with the producer, and the camera men mount their cameras. The lights go up, the 'monitors' are switched on, and 10 seconds before time the studio manager starts a Cape Canaveral type count down, and at zero he cues whoever is to start the programme and we are on the air. At this point one seems to become blissfully unaware of everything outside the ring of cameras and concentrates on what has to be said and done; in what appears to be just a few minutes, the half hour is up and another 'Gardening Club' is complete.
